items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: That is my brother's best friend, him and Freddie. ... I ain't seen him since the time you brought him here. He came by here a year ago. And I sure was glad to see him.

ctx.x: Well he used to play with my brother. Well, he was a good guitar player, manly player, banjo player. He was a string hand, for instance, man. Well, he turned around and I see him and I say, Willie, I says, I says, how about, what is that you're making this now? So, I just have to buy him a little drink or something like that, you know, and I know he used to like his beer and his wine and all that. Well, I, you know, I was working, I had to work, because I never had no music on me, I never had nothing to learn, I…
I know. Manuel Mineta teaches all of those same kind of things. Manuel Mineta? He teaches time like that, too, and all that.

I'm talking about Manuel. That is my brother's best friend, him and Freddie. He used to play violin. When Freddie was playing cornet, he used to be, and him and Freddie, every time you see Freddie, you see him. They used to go at this fellow, what they call Henry Morton. Henry Morton's place, they used to go up on Second and Magazine. Well, that was a fine place. Oh, it was a fine place. I don't know if you heard talk about this fellow here, what they call him again, this here fellow, I can't forget it, I can't,…
